spec.description: Where each country's migrants come from and where its emigrants live, 1990–2024: corridors on the map, in and out as a Sankey, men and women as a pyramid. Read live from UN DESA's International Migrant Stock 2024.

spec.rawSql:
-- Map dataset A: the $top largest corridors of $country, one row per year
-- 1990-2024. UN DESA estimates 8 years; each one holds until the next.
WITH od AS (
  SELECT CAST("Location code of destination" AS INTEGER) AS dest,
         CAST("Location code of origin" AS INTEGER) AS orig,
         regexp_replace("Region, development group, country or area of destination", '\*', '', 'g') AS dest_name,
         regexp_replace("Region, development group, country or area of origin", '\*', '', 'g') AS orig_name,
         COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)(_[12])?$')
  FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_destination_and_origin.xlsx',
                 sheet = 'Table 1', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:AE40000')
  WHERE TRY_CAST("Location code of destination" AS INTEGER) < 900
    AND TRY_CAST("Location code of origin" AS INTEGER) < 900
    AND CAST($country AS INTEGER) = CASE $direction
          WHEN 'emigrants' THEN TRY_CAST("Location code of origin" AS INTEGER)
          ELSE TRY_CAST("Location code of destination" AS INTEGER) END
    -- Only in the arcs view; the flows view leaves the placeholder row below.
    AND $view = 'arcs'
), cells AS (
  UNPIVOT od ON COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE (dest, orig, dest_name, orig_name)) INTO NAME col VALUE v
), flows AS (
  SELECT orig, dest,
         CASE $direction WHEN 'emigrants' THEN dest ELSE orig END AS partner,
         CASE $direction WHEN 'emigrants' THEN dest_name ELSE orig_name END AS partner_name,
         CAST(left(col, 4) AS INTEGER) AS est_year,
         TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) AS people
  FROM cells
  WHERE CASE right(col, 2) WHEN '_1' THEN 'male' WHEN '_2' THEN 'female' ELSE 'both' END = $sex
), ranked AS (
  -- Ties break by name, the same way as the table, so both show the same partners.
  SELECT * FROM flows
  WHERE people > 0
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY est_year ORDER BY people DESC, partner_name) <= CAST($top AS INTEGER)
), ne AS (
  SELECT f.properties.ISO_N3 AS iso_n3, f.properties.ISO_N3_EH AS iso_n3_eh, f.properties.UN_A3 AS un_a3,
         f.properties.NAME AS name, f.properties.POP_EST AS pop_est,
         f.properties.LABEL_X AS lng, f.properties.LABEL_Y AS lat
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/ca96624a56bd078437bca8184e78163e5039ad19/geojson/ne_50m_admin_0_countries.geojson',
                       maximum_object_size = 200000000))
), cent AS (
  -- One centroid per M49 code: ISO_N3 first, then ISO_N3_EH (France and
  -- Norway carry -99 in ISO_N3), then UN_A3, then the label points below.
  -- Within a priority the most populous feature wins (code 36 is both
  -- Australia and Ashmore and Cartier Is.), then the name; lng and lat always
  -- come from the same feature.
  SELECT code, arg_min({'lng': lng, 'lat': lat}, (prio, -pop_est, name)) AS pick
  FROM (SELECT TRY_CAST(iso_n3 AS INTEGER) AS code, 1 AS prio, pop_est, name, lng, lat FROM ne
        UNION ALL SELECT TRY_CAST(iso_n3_eh AS INTEGER), 2, pop_est, name, lng, lat FROM ne
        UNION ALL SELECT TRY_CAST(un_a3 AS INTEGER), 3, pop_est, name, lng, lat FROM ne
        -- Approximate label points, entered by hand, used only for the nine
        -- territories Natural Earth has no match for.
        UNION ALL SELECT code, 4, 0, name, lng, lat
        FROM (VALUES (175, 'Mayotte', 45.14, -12.83), (254, 'French Guiana', -53.13, 3.93),
                     (292, 'Gibraltar', -5.35, 36.14), (312, 'Guadeloupe', -61.58, 16.25),
                     (474, 'Martinique', -61.02, 14.64), (535, 'Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba', -68.26, 12.18),
                     (638, 'Réunion', 55.54, -21.12), (772, 'Tokelau', -171.85, -9.20),
                     (830, 'Channel Islands', -2.35, 49.35)) label_points(code, name, lng, lat))
  WHERE code > 0
  GROUP BY code
), steps AS (
  SELECT r.y AS year, max(est.e) AS est_year
  FROM range(1990, 2025) r(y)
  JOIN (VALUES (1990), (1995), (2000), (2005), (2010), (2015), (2020), (2024)) est(e) ON est.e <= r.y
  GROUP BY r.y
), arcs AS (
  SELECT make_timestamp(s.year, 7, 1, 0, 0, 0) AS time,
         t.partner_name AS partner,
         t.people,
         o.pick.lat AS lat0, o.pick.lng AS lng0,
         d.pick.lat AS lat1, d.pick.lng AS lng1,
         p.pick.lat AS partner_lat, p.pick.lng AS partner_lng,
         t.partner_name || ': ' || CASE
           WHEN t.people >= 999500 THEN printf('%.1fM', t.people / 1e6)
           WHEN t.people >= 1e3 THEN printf('%.0fk', t.people / 1e3)
           ELSE printf('%.0f', t.people) END AS label,
         -- The partner's M49 code: a click on the arc or its label selects that country.
         CAST(t.partner AS VARCHAR) AS code
  FROM steps s
  JOIN ranked t USING (est_year)
  JOIN cent o ON o.code = t.orig
  JOIN cent d ON d.code = t.dest
  JOIN cent p ON p.code = t.partner
)
SELECT * FROM arcs
-- No corridor at all (no immigrants into the Holy See, say): one empty row, so
-- the map replaces the previous country's arcs instead of keeping them.
UNION ALL
SELECT make_timestamp(2024, 7, 1, 0, 0, 0), NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM arcs)
ORDER BY time, people DESC, partner

-- Map dataset B: international migrant stock of every country, one row per
-- country and year 1990-2024, each estimate held until the next.
WITH d AS (
  SELECT CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) AS code,
         regexp_replace("Region, development group, country or area", '\*', '', 'g') AS country,
         COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)(_[12])?$')
  FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_and_destination.xlsx',
                 sheet = 'Table 1', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:AC400')
  WHERE TRY_CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) < 900
), cells AS (
  UNPIVOT d ON COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE (code, country)) INTO NAME col VALUE v
), stock AS (
  SELECT code, country, CAST(left(col, 4) AS INTEGER) AS est_year, TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) AS stock
  FROM cells
  WHERE CASE right(col, 2) WHEN '_1' THEN 'male' WHEN '_2' THEN 'female' ELSE 'both' END = $sex
), ne AS (
  SELECT f.properties.ISO_N3 AS iso_n3, f.properties.ISO_N3_EH AS iso_n3_eh, f.properties.UN_A3 AS un_a3,
         f.properties.NAME AS name, f.properties.POP_EST AS pop_est,
         f.properties.LABEL_X AS lng, f.properties.LABEL_Y AS lat
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/ca96624a56bd078437bca8184e78163e5039ad19/geojson/ne_50m_admin_0_countries.geojson',
                       maximum_object_size = 200000000))
), cent AS (
  -- One centroid per M49 code: ISO_N3 first, then ISO_N3_EH (France and
  -- Norway carry -99 in ISO_N3), then UN_A3, then the label points below.
  -- Within a priority the most populous feature wins (code 36 is both
  -- Australia and Ashmore and Cartier Is.), then the name; lng and lat always
  -- come from the same feature.
  SELECT code, arg_min({'lng': lng, 'lat': lat}, (prio, -pop_est, name)) AS pick
  FROM (SELECT TRY_CAST(iso_n3 AS INTEGER) AS code, 1 AS prio, pop_est, name, lng, lat FROM ne
        UNION ALL SELECT TRY_CAST(iso_n3_eh AS INTEGER), 2, pop_est, name, lng, lat FROM ne
        UNION ALL SELECT TRY_CAST(un_a3 AS INTEGER), 3, pop_est, name, lng, lat FROM ne
        -- Approximate label points, entered by hand, used only for the nine
        -- territories Natural Earth has no match for.
        UNION ALL SELECT code, 4, 0, name, lng, lat
        FROM (VALUES (175, 'Mayotte', 45.14, -12.83), (254, 'French Guiana', -53.13, 3.93),
                     (292, 'Gibraltar', -5.35, 36.14), (312, 'Guadeloupe', -61.58, 16.25),
                     (474, 'Martinique', -61.02, 14.64), (535, 'Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba', -68.26, 12.18),
                     (638, 'Réunion', 55.54, -21.12), (772, 'Tokelau', -171.85, -9.20),
                     (830, 'Channel Islands', -2.35, 49.35)) label_points(code, name, lng, lat))
  WHERE code > 0
  GROUP BY code
), steps AS (
  SELECT r.y AS year, max(est.e) AS est_year
  FROM range(1990, 2025) r(y)
  JOIN (VALUES (1990), (1995), (2000), (2005), (2010), (2015), (2020), (2024)) est(e) ON est.e <= r.y
  GROUP BY r.y
)
SELECT make_timestamp(s.year, 7, 1, 0, 0, 0) AS time,
       k.country,
       k.stock,
       c.pick.lat AS latitude,
       c.pick.lng AS longitude,
       -- The country's M49 code: a click on its bubble selects it.
       CAST(k.code AS VARCHAR) AS code
FROM steps s
JOIN stock k USING (est_year)
JOIN cent c USING (code)
WHERE k.stock > 0
ORDER BY time, k.stock DESC

-- Map dataset C: the $top largest inflows and the $top largest outflows of
-- $country, one row per year 1990-2024, each estimate held until the next.
-- Only in the flows view; in the arcs view one empty row keeps the dataset.
WITH od AS (
  SELECT CAST("Location code of destination" AS INTEGER) AS dest,
         CAST("Location code of origin" AS INTEGER) AS orig,
         regexp_replace("Region, development group, country or area of destination", '\*', '', 'g') AS dest_name,
         regexp_replace("Region, development group, country or area of origin", '\*', '', 'g') AS orig_name,
         COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)(_[12])?$')
  FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_destination_and_origin.xlsx',
                 sheet = 'Table 1', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:AE40000')
  WHERE TRY_CAST("Location code of destination" AS INTEGER) < 900
    AND TRY_CAST("Location code of origin" AS INTEGER) < 900
    AND CAST($country AS INTEGER) IN (TRY_CAST("Location code of destination" AS INTEGER),
                                      TRY_CAST("Location code of origin" AS INTEGER))
    AND $view = 'flows'
), cells AS (
  UNPIVOT od ON COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE (dest, orig, dest_name, orig_name)) INTO NAME col VALUE v
), moves AS (
  SELECT orig, dest,
         CASE WHEN dest = CAST($country AS INTEGER) THEN 'in' ELSE 'out' END AS direction,
         CASE WHEN dest = CAST($country AS INTEGER) THEN orig ELSE dest END AS partner,
         CASE WHEN dest = CAST($country AS INTEGER) THEN orig_name ELSE dest_name END AS partner_name,
         CAST(left(col, 4) AS INTEGER) AS est_year,
         TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) AS people
  FROM cells
  WHERE CASE right(col, 2) WHEN '_1' THEN 'male' WHEN '_2' THEN 'female' ELSE 'both' END = $sex
), ranked AS (
  -- Ties break by name, the same way as the table.
  SELECT * FROM moves
  WHERE people > 0
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY est_year, direction ORDER BY people DESC, partner_name) <= CAST($top AS INTEGER)
), ne AS (
  SELECT f.properties.ISO_N3 AS iso_n3, f.properties.ISO_N3_EH AS iso_n3_eh, f.properties.UN_A3 AS un_a3,
         f.properties.NAME AS name, f.properties.POP_EST AS pop_est,
         f.properties.LABEL_X AS lng, f.properties.LABEL_Y AS lat
  FROM (SELECT unnest(features) AS f
        FROM read_json('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/ca96624a56bd078437bca8184e78163e5039ad19/geojson/ne_50m_admin_0_countries.geojson',
                       maximum_object_size = 200000000))
), cent AS (
  -- The same centroids as corridors.sql and bubbles.sql.
  SELECT code, arg_min({'lng': lng, 'lat': lat}, (prio, -pop_est, name)) AS pick
  FROM (SELECT TRY_CAST(iso_n3 AS INTEGER) AS code, 1 AS prio, pop_est, name, lng, lat FROM ne
        UNION ALL SELECT TRY_CAST(iso_n3_eh AS INTEGER), 2, pop_est, name, lng, lat FROM ne
        UNION ALL SELECT TRY_CAST(un_a3 AS INTEGER), 3, pop_est, name, lng, lat FROM ne
        UNION ALL SELECT code, 4, 0, name, lng, lat
        FROM (VALUES (175, 'Mayotte', 45.14, -12.83), (254, 'French Guiana', -53.13, 3.93),
                     (292, 'Gibraltar', -5.35, 36.14), (312, 'Guadeloupe', -61.58, 16.25),
                     (474, 'Martinique', -61.02, 14.64), (535, 'Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba', -68.26, 12.18),
                     (638, 'Réunion', 55.54, -21.12), (772, 'Tokelau', -171.85, -9.20),
                     (830, 'Channel Islands', -2.35, 49.35)) label_points(code, name, lng, lat))
  WHERE code > 0
  GROUP BY code
), steps AS (
  SELECT r.y AS year, max(est.e) AS est_year
  FROM range(1990, 2025) r(y)
  JOIN (VALUES (1990), (1995), (2000), (2005), (2010), (2015), (2020), (2024)) est(e) ON est.e <= r.y
  GROUP BY r.y
), flows AS (
  SELECT make_timestamp(s.year, 7, 1, 0, 0, 0) AS time,
         t.direction,
         t.partner_name AS partner,
         CAST(t.partner AS VARCHAR) AS code,
         t.people AS count,
         o.pick.lat AS lat0, o.pick.lng AS lng0,
         d.pick.lat AS lat1, d.pick.lng AS lng1
  FROM steps s
  JOIN ranked t USING (est_year)
  JOIN cent o ON o.code = t.orig
  JOIN cent d ON d.code = t.dest
)
SELECT * FROM flows
UNION ALL
SELECT make_timestamp(2024, 7, 1, 0, 0, 0), NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM flows)
ORDER BY time, direction, count DESC, partner

spec.description: Largest corridors of the selected country (arcs) over every country's international migrant stock (grey). Click a country to select it. Map view swaps the arcs for flows in both directions. Play the clock or narrow it to a year.
spec.title: Migrant corridors

spec.rawSql:
-- Key figures for $country at the estimate in force on the map clock. The
-- clock window's end is exclusive, hence the millisecond.
WITH clock AS (
  SELECT max(est.e) AS est_year
  FROM (VALUES (1990), (1995), (2000), (2005), (2010), (2015), (2020), (2024)) est(e)
  WHERE est.e <= greatest(1990, COALESCE(year(TRY_CAST(NULLIF($mapTo, '') AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL 1 MILLISECOND), 2024))
), sel AS (
  SELECT est_year,
         CAST(est_year AS VARCHAR) AS col_both,
         CAST(est_year AS VARCHAR) || CASE $sex WHEN 'male' THEN '_1' WHEN 'female' THEN '_2' ELSE '' END AS col
  FROM clock
), stock AS (
  UNPIVOT (SELECT COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)(_[12])?$')
           FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_and_destination.xlsx',
                          sheet = 'Table 1', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:AC400')
           WHERE TRY_CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) = CAST($country AS INTEGER))
  ON COLUMNS(*) INTO NAME col VALUE v
), share AS (
  UNPIVOT (SELECT COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)(_[12])?$')
           FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_and_destination.xlsx',
                          sheet = 'Table 3', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:AC400')
           WHERE TRY_CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) = CAST($country AS INTEGER))
  ON COLUMNS(*) INTO NAME col VALUE v
), female AS (
  UNPIVOT (SELECT COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)$')
           FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_and_destination.xlsx',
                          sheet = 'Table 4', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:M400')
           WHERE TRY_CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) = CAST($country AS INTEGER))
  ON COLUMNS(*) INTO NAME col VALUE v
), emigrants AS (
  UNPIVOT (SELECT COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)(_[12])?$')
           FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_and_origin.xlsx',
                          sheet = 'Table 1', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:AC400')
           WHERE TRY_CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) = CAST($country AS INTEGER))
  ON COLUMNS(*) INTO NAME col VALUE v
)
SELECT sel.est_year AS "Estimate year",
       (SELECT TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) FROM stock WHERE stock.col = sel.col) AS "International migrants",
       (SELECT TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) FROM share WHERE share.col = sel.col) AS "Share of population",
       (SELECT TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) FROM female WHERE female.col = sel.col_both) AS "Share female",
       (SELECT TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) FROM emigrants WHERE emigrants.col = sel.col) AS "Emigrants"
FROM sel

spec.description: UN DESA estimate in force at the year on the map's clock. Share female is for both sexes.
spec.title: Key figures

spec.rawSql:
-- The $top largest origins of $country's immigrants and the $top largest
-- destinations of its emigrants, at the estimate in force on the map clock,
-- each with its share of that side's total (the World row, code 900). Ties
-- break by name, the same way as the map.
WITH clock AS (
  SELECT max(est.e) AS est_year
  FROM (VALUES (1990), (1995), (2000), (2005), (2010), (2015), (2020), (2024)) est(e)
  WHERE est.e <= greatest(1990, COALESCE(year(TRY_CAST(NULLIF($mapTo, '') AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL 1 MILLISECOND), 2024))
), sel AS (
  SELECT CAST(est_year AS VARCHAR) || CASE $sex WHEN 'male' THEN '_1' WHEN 'female' THEN '_2' ELSE '' END AS col
  FROM clock
), od AS (
  SELECT CAST("Location code of destination" AS INTEGER) AS dest,
         CAST("Location code of origin" AS INTEGER) AS orig,
         regexp_replace("Region, development group, country or area of destination", '\*', '', 'g') AS dest_name,
         regexp_replace("Region, development group, country or area of origin", '\*', '', 'g') AS orig_name,
         COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)(_[12])?$')
  FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_destination_and_origin.xlsx',
                 sheet = 'Table 1', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:AE40000')
  WHERE CAST($country AS INTEGER) IN (TRY_CAST("Location code of destination" AS INTEGER),
                                      TRY_CAST("Location code of origin" AS INTEGER))
), cells AS (
  UNPIVOT od ON COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE (dest, orig, dest_name, orig_name)) INTO NAME col VALUE v
), moves AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN dest = CAST($country AS INTEGER) THEN 'in' ELSE 'out' END AS side,
         CASE WHEN dest = CAST($country AS INTEGER) THEN orig ELSE dest END AS partner,
         CASE WHEN dest = CAST($country AS INTEGER) THEN orig_name ELSE dest_name END AS partner_name,
         TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) AS people
  FROM cells
  JOIN sel USING (col)
), totals AS (
  SELECT side, people AS total FROM moves WHERE partner = 900
)
SELECT side,
       CAST(partner AS VARCHAR) AS code,
       partner_name AS name,
       people,
       round(100 * people / total, 1) AS share
FROM moves
JOIN totals USING (side)
WHERE partner < 900 AND people > 0
QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY side ORDER BY people DESC, partner_name) <= CAST($top AS INTEGER)
ORDER BY side, people DESC, name

spec.description: Largest origins of the country's immigrants (left) and destinations of its emigrants (right), at the year on the map's clock. Click a country to select it.
spec.title: Corridors in and out

spec.rawSql:
-- Men and women in the $top largest corridors of $country ($direction), at the
-- estimate in force on the map clock. Ranked by both sexes, like the table.
WITH clock AS (
  SELECT max(est.e) AS est_year
  FROM (VALUES (1990), (1995), (2000), (2005), (2010), (2015), (2020), (2024)) est(e)
  WHERE est.e <= greatest(1990, COALESCE(year(TRY_CAST(NULLIF($mapTo, '') AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL 1 MILLISECOND), 2024))
), od AS (
  SELECT CAST("Location code of destination" AS INTEGER) AS dest,
         CAST("Location code of origin" AS INTEGER) AS orig,
         regexp_replace("Region, development group, country or area of destination", '\*', '', 'g') AS dest_name,
         regexp_replace("Region, development group, country or area of origin", '\*', '', 'g') AS orig_name,
         COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)(_[12])?$')
  FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_destination_and_origin.xlsx',
                 sheet = 'Table 1', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:AE40000')
  WHERE CAST($country AS INTEGER) = CASE $direction
          WHEN 'emigrants' THEN TRY_CAST("Location code of origin" AS INTEGER)
          ELSE TRY_CAST("Location code of destination" AS INTEGER) END
    AND CASE $direction
          WHEN 'emigrants' THEN TRY_CAST("Location code of destination" AS INTEGER)
          ELSE TRY_CAST("Location code of origin" AS INTEGER) END < 900
), cells AS (
  UNPIVOT od ON COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE (dest, orig, dest_name, orig_name)) INTO NAME col VALUE v
), wide AS (
  SELECT CASE $direction WHEN 'emigrants' THEN dest ELSE orig END AS partner,
         CASE $direction WHEN 'emigrants' THEN dest_name ELSE orig_name END AS partner_name,
         max(TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE)) FILTER (WHERE length(col) = 4) AS both_sexes,
         max(TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE)) FILTER (WHERE right(col, 2) = '_1') AS men,
         max(TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE)) FILTER (WHERE right(col, 2) = '_2') AS women
  FROM cells, clock
  WHERE CAST(left(col, 4) AS INTEGER) = clock.est_year
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT partner_name AS "Country", CAST(partner AS VARCHAR) AS code, men AS "Men", women AS "Women"
FROM wide
WHERE both_sexes > 0
ORDER BY both_sexes DESC, partner_name
LIMIT CAST($top AS INTEGER)

spec.description: Men (left) and women (right) in the country's largest corridors, for the Direction picker and the year on the map's clock, with each one's share of women. Click a bar to select that country.
spec.title: Men and women by corridor

spec.rawSql:
-- International migrants as a share of the population, $country against the
-- World, at the 8 years UN DESA actually estimates. PIVOT names each column
-- after the country, so the legend needs no override.
WITH d AS (
  SELECT CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) AS code,
         regexp_replace("Region, development group, country or area", '\*', '', 'g') AS name,
         COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)(_[12])?$')
  FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_and_destination.xlsx',
                 sheet = 'Table 3', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:AC400')
  WHERE TRY_CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) IN (900, CAST($country AS INTEGER))
), cells AS (
  UNPIVOT d ON COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE (code, name)) INTO NAME col VALUE v
), points AS (
  SELECT make_timestamp(CAST(left(col, 4) AS INTEGER), 7, 1, 0, 0, 0) AS time,
         name,
         TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) AS share
  FROM cells
  WHERE CASE right(col, 2) WHEN '_1' THEN 'male' WHEN '_2' THEN 'female' ELSE 'both' END = $sex
)
SELECT * FROM (PIVOT points ON name USING first(share) GROUP BY time)
ORDER BY time

spec.description: Only the eight years UN DESA estimates; no step.

spec.rawSql:
-- The share of women among $country's immigrants (UN DESA Table 4 by
-- destination) and among its emigrants (Table 1 by origin, women over both
-- sexes), with the World for reference: the world's immigrants and emigrants
-- are the same people, so one line serves both.
WITH immigrants AS (
  UNPIVOT (SELECT CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) AS code,
                  COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)$')
           FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_and_destination.xlsx',
                          sheet = 'Table 4', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:M400')
           WHERE TRY_CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) IN (900, CAST($country AS INTEGER)))
  ON COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE (code)) INTO NAME col VALUE v
), emigrants AS (
  UNPIVOT (SELECT COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)(_2)?$')
           FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_and_origin.xlsx',
                          sheet = 'Table 1', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:AC400')
           WHERE TRY_CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) = CAST($country AS INTEGER))
  ON COLUMNS(*) INTO NAME col VALUE v
), points AS (
  SELECT CAST(left(col, 4) AS INTEGER) AS year,
         CASE WHEN code = 900 THEN 'World' ELSE 'Among immigrants' END AS series,
         TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) AS share
  FROM immigrants
  UNION ALL
  SELECT CAST(left(col, 4) AS INTEGER),
         'Among emigrants',
         100 * max(TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE)) FILTER (WHERE right(col, 2) = '_2')
             / max(TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE)) FILTER (WHERE length(col) = 4)
  FROM emigrants
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT * FROM (
  PIVOT (SELECT make_timestamp(year, 7, 1, 0, 0, 0) AS time, series, share FROM points)
  ON series USING first(share) GROUP BY time
)
ORDER BY time

spec.description: Share of women among the country's immigrants and emigrants at UN DESA's eight estimate years, with the world share for reference (the world's immigrants and emigrants are the same people).
spec.title: Women among migrants · ${country:text}

options.content:
**Source.** United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). *International Migrant Stock 2024.* [un.org](https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/content/international-migrant-stock) · [CC BY 3.0 IGO](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/igo/). Adapted: estimates carried forward between UN DESA's estimate years; country names without footnote marks. Centroids: Natural Earth.

**Reading the map.** UN DESA estimates 1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2024. The clock steps through every year and shows the latest estimate at or before it, so the map changes only in those eight years. Arcs run from origin (orange) to destination (teal). Click a bubble, an arc or a label to select that country; a click on the sea keeps the current one. Right-drag to tilt or rotate. Map view swaps the arcs for flows in both directions: arrows show the direction, widths the people, rings each country's totals.

**Reading the charts.** *Corridors in and out* sets the largest origins of the country's immigrants (teal, left) against the largest destinations of its emigrants (orange, right), whatever the Direction picker says; widths are people. *Men and women by corridor* follows the Direction picker. Click a country in either chart to select it, as on the map.

**Live data.** Every panel reads the UN DESA spreadsheets when it loads, so the dashboard takes a few seconds. Pause the clock to update the key figures and the charts.

spec.__legacyStringValue:
-- Only countries with at least one estimate: Saint Barthélemy and Saint Martin
-- (French part) have a row, but every year column is empty.
SELECT regexp_replace("Region, development group, country or area", '\*', '', 'g') AS __text,
       CAST(CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) AS VARCHAR) AS __value
FROM read_xlsx('https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_and_destination.xlsx',
               sheet = 'Table 1', header = true, all_varchar = true, range = 'A11:AC400')
WHERE TRY_CAST("Location code" AS INTEGER) < 900
  AND len(list_filter([COLUMNS('^(1990|1995|2000|2005|2010|2015|2020|2024)(_[12])?$')],
                      v -> TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL)) > 0
ORDER BY __text COLLATE NOACCENT
